data.title: The LKB1 tumor suppressor negatively regulates mTOR signaling
data.authors: Shaw RJ; Bardeesy N; Manning BD; Lopez L; Kosmatka M; DePinho RA; Cantley LC

evidence.label: Molecular — cells, biochemistry, structure
evidence.note: this describes the kind of study, not its quality

data.model_system: Lkb1-null mouse embryonic fibroblasts; cultured cells under low ATP; gastrointestinal polyps from Lkb1 mutant mice
data.finding: Reported that LKB1 is needed to switch mTOR signalling off when cellular ATP falls, and that this requires AMPK and TSC2. Lkb1-null fibroblasts and the hamartomatous gut polyps of Lkb1 mutant mice showed raised signalling downstream of mTOR. The authors proposed mTOR inhibitors as a treatment idea for Peutz-Jeghers syndrome. Published alongside Corradetti et al. 2004, which reached the same LKB1-AMPK-TSC2 link independently. Boundary: worked from the abstract only (no PMC full text); cell and mouse data, the treatment suggestion was not tested here.
data.abstract_excerpt: Germline mutations in LKB1, TSC2, or PTEN tumor suppressor genes result in hamartomatous syndromes with shared tumor biological features. The recent observations of LKB1-mediated activation of AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK) and AMPK inhibition of mTOR through TSC2 prompted us to examine the biochemical and biological relationship between LKB1 and mTOR regulation.

extracted_findings.species: Mouse embryonic fibroblasts; Lkb1 mutant mice
extracted_findings.effect: Loss of LKB1 prevents repression of mTOR under low ATP and raises mTOR signalling in polyps

extracted_findings_review.note: AI-assisted extraction from the paper. The curated finding takes precedence where the two disagree.
